## Long-term Knowledge

### Architecture

<!-- lore:019ea9c2-23e7-78a3-b559-416743674bc7 -->
* **Docs-site structure: Zod .describe() + generator + check-docs CI job**: Configuration docs at \`packages/website/src/content/docs/docs/configuration.md\` are auto-generated from \`packages/core/src/config.ts\` Zod schemas. Pipeline: add \`.describe()\` to Zod fields → \`scripts/generate-config-docs.ts\` walks \`.shape\` + \`.description\` (with \`unwrap()\` for defaults/checks) → emits markdown with YAML frontmatter, \`##\` top-level, \`###\` nested, tables (Field|Type|Default|Constraints|Description) → wired via \`pnpm generate:docs\` and \`pnpm check:docs\` (root \`package.json\`) → \`check-docs\` CI job runs \`tsx scripts/generate-config-docs.ts --check\` to fail on drift. Mirrors Sentry CLI pattern (\`script/generate-command-docs.ts\` + \`script/generate-docs-sections.ts\` with \`--check\` flag for CI dry-run). Sidebar Reference group added in \`astro.config.mjs\`.

<!-- lore:019e6904-e0e1-7689-bb52-7e8a0cb0edda -->
* **Gateway recall: Marker-and-Expand strategy — tool injection, interception, and round-trip**: Recall tool injected by gateway pipeline (pipeline.ts), NOT OpenCode plugin. Injection condition: \`modifiedReq.tools.length > 0 && !clientHasRecallTool(tools)\`. Strategy: (1) Response: recall \`tool\_use\` replaced with marker text via \`replaceRecallWithMarker()\`; result stored in \`sessionState.recallStore\`. (2) Next request: \`expandRecallMarkers()\` restores \`tool\_use\`+\`tool\_result\` pairs before forwarding. \`buildRecallFollowUp()\`: assistant message = ORIGINAL \`tool\_use\` block; user message = \`tool\_result\` block with recall results (NOT plain text) — prevents LLM echoing raw recall formatting during streaming. \`hasContinuationAfter\` logic: if blocks follow marker, truncates/splices; else prepends tool\_result to next user msg. \`RecallAwareAccumulator\` suppresses recall SSE blocks. MAX\_RECALL\_DEPTH=10. Follow-up requests: \`cacheConversation: false\`.

<!-- lore:019ea9c2-c48c-769e-8e1f-c2061314d685 -->
* **getWorkerModel() same-provider invariant and dynamic discovery**: Worker/warmup model ALWAYS uses same provider as session. \`getWorkerModel()\` fallback chain: (1) cfg.model, (2) sessionModelID (any provider — same provider is always safe), (3) WORKER\_DEFAULTS\[effectiveProvider], (4) undefined. For known providers (anthropic, openai), cost-aware defaults downgrade to cheaper models when inputCost >= EXPENSIVE\_MODEL\_THRESHOLD. For unknown providers, \`findCheaperSameProviderModel()\` dynamically searches models.dev cache for a cheaper same-provider model; if none found, echoes the session model. Cross-provider guard in pipeline.ts detects model/upstream provider mismatch at prompt time, calls \`recordWorkerFailure('cross-provider')\` + returns null. Workers must NEVER fall back to \`config().model\`/\`cfg.model\` — \`const model = input.model\` with NO fallback is correct in curator.ts, distillation.ts, pattern-echo.ts.

<!-- lore:019e7013-a9ea-72e6-8e8c-17ef1848e4e0 -->
* **llm-adapter.ts: retry logic, backoff schedule, and circuit breaker integration**: llm-adapter.ts retry/backoff: \`TRANSIENT\_CODES={429,500,502,503,529}\`; \`AUTH\_ERROR\_CODES={401,403}\`. \`MAX\_RETRIES\_RATE\_LIMIT=3\`; \`MAX\_RETRIES\_SERVER=3\`; \`MAX\_RETRIES\_URGENT=2\`. \`backoffMs()\`: Retry-After present → \`min(retryAfterMs, cap)\`; urgent → \`min(1000×2^attempt, 4000)\`; 429 non-urgent → \`min(60\_000+attempt×60\_000, 180\_000)\`; 5xx → \`min(1000×2^attempt, 8000)\`. On 429 non-urgent → \`tripCircuitBreaker(pauseSec)\`. Auth errors → \`markAuthStale\`, re-resolve, retry once if \`credentialChanged && attempt===0\`. \`buildAnthropicWorkerRequest()\`: injects billing block only when \`cred.scheme === 'bearer'\`; system sent as block array with \`cache\_control: { type: 'ephemeral', ttl: '1h' }\`; body signed via \`signBody()\`. \`opts.thinking\` intentionally NOT forwarded in bare API fetch. Sentry init: \`packages/gateway/instrument.ts\`; polyfill \`util.getSystemErrorMap = () => new Map()\` BEFORE \`Sentry.init()\` (Bun's node:util lacks it).

<!-- lore:019ea9c2-23fc-76c9-9fce-1982674d649f -->
* **LORE\_UPSTREAM\_EXTRA\_HEADERS: env-driven config + parser + merge**: LORE\_UPSTREAM\_EXTRA\_HEADERS: env-driven config + parser + merge (Phase 0, June 2026): curl-style parser (\`parse-curl-headers\` in \`packages/gateway/src/config.ts\`) handles comma-separated \`Key: Value\` pairs. \`applyUpstreamExtraHeaders\` merges caller headers with LORE\_UPSTREAM\_EXTRA\_HEADERS overlay (caller wins, env fills gaps, lowercase key normalization). Applied at 5 sites: 3 builders in pipeline.ts, snapshot, handleModelsPassthrough, executeWarmup, passthroughResponsesCompact. Codex agents.ts folds into \`-c openai\_provider\_headers = { ... }\` (TOML-escaped). OpenCode plugin reads both LORE\_UPSTREAM\_\<PROVIDER> and LORE\_UPSTREAM\_EXTRA\_HEADERS. 23 new tests (13 parser + 6 merge + 4 codex). 85 files / 2320 tests passing.

<!-- lore:019e54f5-04be-7a9f-9e62-177d65d5db9f -->
* **LTM forSession() budget, phases, and safety-net constants**: LTM forSession() architecture: \`forSession()\` (ltm.ts) budgets: \`budget.ltm\`=0.05, \`budget.preferenceLtm\`=0.02. Phases: (1) architecture entries up to ARCH\_BUDGET\_FRACTION=0.2; (2) remaining by score desc; (3) .lore.md sections. HEADER\_OVERHEAD\_TOKENS=15 subtracted upfront. Hard cap: \`if (used+cost>maxTokens) continue\`. PROJECT\_SAFETY\_NET=5: top-confidence project entries ALWAYS included even with zero relevance score. NO\_CONTEXT\_FALLBACK\_CAP=10. Global entries (pid=null) must be cross\_project=1. Pool SQL: project pool uses \`cross\_project=0\`; cross pool uses \`project\_id IS NULL OR cross\_project=1\`. Promoted entries (cross\_project=1) lose PROJECT\_SAFETY\_NET guarantee in home project. GOTCHA: \`vectorSearch()\` queries \`knowledge WHERE embedding IS NOT NULL AND confidence>0.2\` — test suites must \`DELETE FROM knowledge WHERE embedding IS NOT NULL\` in beforeEach. Dedup threshold for Nomic v1.5 is 0.935.

<!-- lore:019ea9c2-c495-7d28-8a72-0eea649d1d41 -->
* **models.dev fetch loads ALL providers, not just anthropic/openai**: The \`fetchModelData()\` function in \`worker-model.ts\` iterates ALL providers in the models.dev \`api.json\` response (not just the hardcoded \`SUPPORTED\_PROVIDERS = \['anthropic', 'openai']\`). This enables cost-aware worker model selection for any provider (MiniMax, Google, xAI, etc.). \`cachedProviderModels\` stores a provider→modelIDs index for \`findCheaperSameProviderModel()\`. Cache TTL is 1 hour. \`SUPPORTED\_PROVIDERS\` is kept only to warn when core providers are missing from the response.

<!-- lore:1cdad2a4-5637-471b-a5cb-39c919fb1592 -->
* **Multilingual support: FTS tokenizer, Unicode tokenization, and non-English fallbacks**: Lore supports non-English (e.g. Turkish) conversations. Key design: (1) FTS5 uses \`tokenize='unicode61 remove\_diacritics 0'\` (NOT \`porter\` — English-only stemmer; NOT diacritic-folding — Turkish ç/ğ/ı/ö/ş/ü are distinct letters). Migration v32 rebuilds all 6 FTS tables. (2) \`filterTerms()\`/\`extractTopTerms()\` in \`search.ts\` strip via \`/\[^\p{L}\p{N}\_\s]/gu\` (Unicode-aware) so Turkish words don't split at special letters. Underscore kept for snake\_case. (3) \`pattern-extract.ts\` regexes need NO translation — they run on the LLM observer's \*English-normalized\* output. (4) Two raw-user-text regex sites have a structural fallback: \`hasNonAsciiLetters()\` (exported from \`instruction-detect.ts\`) gates fallbacks in \`extractInstructionCandidates\` (emit whole message as candidate) and \`detectAssertions\` (pin first sentence) — requires ≥3 non-ASCII letters to avoid false positives on English loanwords (café, naïve). (5) \`ltm.rerankPreferences()\` no longer demotes entries lacking English directive words to 0.8. KNOWN LIMITATIONS (deferred): English \`STOPWORDS\` not filtered for other languages (vector+RRF compensates); ~3-4 chars/token estimate is English-tuned (fine for Turkish, off for CJK).

<!-- lore:019e16fc-4410-7424-8a8a-712db1934a44 -->
* **opencode cumulative branch tracks upstream dev with custom patches**: opencode cumulative branch rebases on \`origin/dev\`. Custom patches: (1) plan mode markdown display with collapsible modal in \`plan\_exit\` tool, (2) collapsible question modal/dock (\`origin/collapse-questions\`, not yet merged to dev), (3) unarchive stickiness fix, (4) plan\_exit/plan\_enter deny rules for subagents in task.ts tools map. Upstream renamed \`session/index.ts\` → \`session/session.ts\`. Upstream removed \`cleanupSessionCaches\` from \`session.updated\` (only \`session.deleted\` remains). During rebase, task.ts conflicts: keep upstream's \`deriveSubagentSessionPermission\`, add plan\_exit/plan\_enter inline permission checks in tools map region. Session-level deny alone is insufficient — must also deny in tools map passed to \`SessionPrompt.prompt()\`.

<!-- lore:019e99ac-28eb-7a7f-a362-37e2a18eaec5 -->
* **Session auth cross-contamination: per-provider credential and upstream snapshot fix**: Session auth cross-contamination fix: \`SessionState.lastUpstream\` and \`sessionAuth\` are singular — overwritten when user switches providers mid-conversation. Fix: (1) \`upstreamByProvider: Map\<string, UpstreamSnapshot>\` added to \`SessionState\`; \`lastUpstream\` kept as convenience pointer. (2) \`sessionAuth\` → \`Map\<sessionID, Map\<providerID, AuthCredential>>\`; \`setSessionAuth\`/\`resolveAuth\` take optional \`providerID\`; \`\_default\` slot synced on every write. (3) Session-aware LLM wrapper looks up \`state.upstreamByProvider.get(workerProviderID)\`, falls back to \`state.lastUpstream\`. KNOWN LIMITATIONS: Provider ID namespace mismatch — \`upstreamByProvider\` keys from \`X-Lore-Provider\` header vs \`WORKER\_DEFAULTS\` providerID; MiniMax-only sessions fall back to \`lastUpstream\`. \`getWorkerAuth\` type annotation at pipeline.ts:898 is stale.

<!-- lore:019e5922-4280-76aa-9b79-5ebeae433d7a -->
* **Sub-agent session detection, isolation, and differential treatment**: Sub-agent session detection and isolation: detected via \`x-parent-session-id\` header (pipeline.ts:2773-2809). Each sub-agent gets independent session: temporal storage, gradient state, distillation pipeline, LTM injection, cost tracking. Key differential treatment: (1) cache warming ALWAYS skipped — \`shouldWarm()\` returns false unconditionally; (2) \`findRotationPredecessor()\` skips sub-agents from Tier 1b rotation; (3) idle distillation/curation runs normally. \`isSubagent\`/\`parentSessionId\` persisted to DB (migration v26). Dashboard: collapsible cost-rollup tree via \`loadParentChildMap()\` + \`buildLiveSessionRows()\`; \`rollUp()\` propagates grandchildren costs bottom-up. \*\*OpenCode plugin gap\*\*: \`chat.headers\` hook injects \`x-lore-session-id\` and \`x-lore-agent\` but does NOT set \`x-parent-session-id\` — gateway can't distinguish parent from sub-agent.

<!-- lore:019ea9bb-8a30-7e43-9e82-2e63a76cbc7f -->
* **swift-harbor: cch-seed-check.yml is the Sentry-CLI-style precedent**: cch-seed-check.yml (110 lines) is the existing precedent for Sentry-CLI-style auto-generated content + auto-PR. Pattern: scheduled cron \`0 \*/6 \* \* \*\` + workflow\_dispatch with force-version input. Two jobs: (1) check-version runs scripts/check-cc-version.ts (npm query, exits 1 on miss, --json), (2) extract-seed needs check-version, runs scripts/extract-cch-seed.ts, pins WORKER\_VERSION for latest / --no-pin for backfill, commits to branch cch-seed/${LATEST\_VERSION}, opens PR via \`gh pr create\` titled "feat(cch): add seeds for Claude Code up to ${LATEST\_VERSION}" updating packages/gateway/src/cch.ts. Method: Oracle pair generation via local capture server + binary scan. This is the template to copy for any future auto-generated docs/fragments/AGENTS.md-content workflows. Lines 191-192 are git commit+push; lines 162-209 are the full pattern.

* **X-Lore-\* headers: project path injection and resolution priority**: X-Lore-\* headers and project path resolution: Priority in \`packages/gateway/src/config.ts\`: 1) \`X-Lore-Project\` header (absolute path, max 1024 chars, strips trailing slashes/control chars), 2) inferred from system prompt (\`cwd\` JSON key, \`Working directory:\` prefix, \`.lore.md\` path, generic \`/home/\`/\`/Users/\` paths), 3) \`process.cwd()\` fallback. Source tagged as \`ProjectPathSource\`: \`"header"|"inferred"|"cwd"\`. Pipeline warns on \`cwd\` source (dedup via \`cwdWarned\` Set). \`agents.ts\` \`envVars()\` injects \`X-Lore-Project\` + \`X-Lore-Git-Remote\` into \`ANTHROPIC\_CUSTOM\_HEADERS\`. \*\*Invariants (HIGH-PRIORITY, user directive)\*\*: (a) Confident path (source \`header\` or \`inferred\`) ALWAYS binds & clears provisional binding — overrides any prior state. (b) \`cwd\` NEVER overwrites a confident binding (pipeline.ts:1067-1070). (c) Side-channel sessions that never send the header NEVER self-recover — require bucketing/self-heal. (d) Gateway cwd must never appear as a project (test invariant: \`expect(projects.some(p=>p.path===process.cwd())).toBe(false)\`).

### Gotcha

<!-- lore:019e6a44-dbf1-7df6-ba60-94f75c21b81d -->
* **consolidationUser() batchTarget frame-of-reference mismatch: global target vs batch count produces negative excess**: Trap: \`batchTarget\` in batched consolidation was computed globally (\`Math.max(cfg.curator.maxEntries, entries.length - CONSOLIDATION\_BATCH\_SIZE/2)\` = 1118 for 1143 entries) but \`consolidationUser()\` computed \`excess = count - targetMax\` where \`count\` is the batch size (50). Result: \`excess = 50 - 1118 = -1068\` — prompt tells LLM 'must remove at least -1068 entries', LLM returns empty ops, idle scheduler enters 1h cooldown, system never converges. Fix: \`batchTarget\` must be batch-relative — \`Math.ceil(CONSOLIDATION\_BATCH\_SIZE / 2)\` so \`excess = 50 - 25 = 25\`. Fixed in e8a73f9. CONSOLIDATION\_BATCH\_SIZE=50 (curator.ts:643). Non-batched path (entries ≤ BATCH\_SIZE) correctly uses \`cfg.curator.maxEntries\` as target. Note: \`consolidate()\` NEVER creates entries — only 'update' and 'delete' ops applied; \`includeCross=false\` excludes cross-project entries.

<!-- lore:019e6a1b-3408-7609-ba6b-d4ba9d552afd -->
* **curator.ts applyOps(): create op missing content field crashes at line 226 — filterOps() doesn't validate required fields**: curator.ts applyOps(): create op missing content field crashes at line 226 — filterOps() doesn't validate required fields: Trap: \`filterOps()\` (curator.ts:109–117) only checks \`op\` is a string — does NOT validate required fields (\`content\`, \`title\`, \`category\`) for \`create\` ops, casting result as \`CuratorOp\[]\` silencing TypeScript. When LLM emits a malformed \`create\` op missing \`content\`, \`applyOps()\` line 226 accesses \`op.content.length\` without null guard → \`TypeError: undefined is not an object\`. Fix: add null guard at line 226 AND field validation in \`filterOps()\` for \`create\` ops. The \`update\` branch at line 252 already has \`op.content !== undefined &&\` guard — \`create\` branch lacks equivalent. \`applyOps()\` calls \`ltm.syncRefs(id)\` and \`entities.syncEntityRefs(id, content)\` after each create/update; \`skipCreate\` flag skips creates (used by consolidation); cross-project guard prevents mutating foreign-project entries. \`cfg\` is in scope in \`runInner\` at line 414.

<!-- lore:019ea9c2-c4a3-7073-b1d1-1bcddb6f5f2b -->
* **findCheaperSameProviderModel: falsy check skips zero-cost models**: Trap: \`!entry?.cost?.input\` looks correct for 'no cost data' but \`0\` is falsy — free/zero-priced models are incorrectly excluded as cheaper candidates. Fix: use \`entry?.cost?.input == null\` (null/undefined check) instead of \`!entry?.cost?.input\`. This was fixed in PR #623. Also: dynamic cheaper-model search only runs when \`inputCost >= EXPENSIVE\_MODEL\_THRESHOLD\` — cheap session models always echo without searching.

<!-- lore:019e69f0-a05a-7d48-8e35-76baf13533c5 -->
* **LOREAI-GATEWAY-1E: resp.usage undefined crash in postResponse() for vLLM/OpenAI path**: Trap: \`GatewayUsage\` typed as non-optional on \`GatewayResponse\`, so \`resp.usage.inputTokens\` looks safe. But \`resp.usage\` can be \`undefined\` at runtime (e.g., vLLM returning partial response). All four accumulators construct \`usage\` with \`?? 0\` guards on individual fields — but \`resp.usage\` itself can still be undefined if an exception produces a partial response object. Crash sites: pipeline.ts lines 2069, 2101, 2137-2140, 2150-2153, 2204-2206, 2282-2285, 2341, 2363, 2402; also \`buildOpenAINonStreamResponse\` (openai.ts:296-300). Fix: add \`const usage = resp.usage ?? { inputTokens: 0, outputTokens: 0, cacheReadInputTokens: 0, cacheCreationInputTokens: 0 }\` guard at top of \`postResponse()\` and \`nonStreamHttpResponse()\`, then use \`usage.\*\` throughout.

<!-- lore:019e8d03-3fdf-76cf-b87d-eab142cad8b1 -->
* **OpenAI protocol: split tool messages + recall leak on streaming path**: Two OpenAI-protocol bugs fixed: (1) translate/openai.ts pushed separate user messages per tool\_result msg — breaks Pass 2 which only checks role. Fix: coalesce consecutive tool messages into one user message. (2) OpenAI/openai-responses streaming dispatch accumulated upstream SSE then returned early, skipping the recall loop. Fix: recall closure called from all three accumulated-response paths. Also: recall.ts must set content-type override — follow-ups parsed as JSON via streaming clients; without override, SSE→JSON parse crash occurs.

<!-- lore:019e4eab-59b4-7fe3-be03-874f682cc340 -->
* **openai.ts: array-format content in system/developer messages silently dropped**: openai.ts / openai-responses.ts parsing traps: (1) \`parseOpenAIRequest\` coerces non-string content to \`""\` — FIXED in PR #526: array-format system/developer content now extracts text parts. (2) \`buildOpenAIMessages\` (openai.ts:523–529): \`tool\_result\` blocks pushed mid-loop before \`textParts\`/\`toolUses\` flushed — tool\_result appears before text/tool\_use of same message. (3) \`buildOpenAIMessages\` always re-emits system as \`role:'system'\`, never \`'developer'\`. (4) \`parseOpenAIResponsesRequest\` reads system prompt from top-level \`instructions\` field. (5) \`item\_reference\` and \`reasoning\` items in \`parseInputItems\` silently dropped. \`store\` field not in extras allow-list — silently dropped. LTM injection for Responses API: \`\[req.system, cache?.stableLtmSystem, cache?.ltmSystem].filter(Boolean).join('\n\n')\`. \`buildOpenAIMessages\`: uses array content form only when \`hasOpaque=true\` (multimodal), plain string otherwise (cache stability). Consecutive role:"tool" messages coalesced into one user message.

<!-- lore:019ea9c2-c49c-7a85-8e17-16d4e11566d7 -->
* **query expansion 'timed out or failed' on unknown-provider sessions is expected behavior**: Trap: \`\[lore] query expansion timed out or failed, using original query\` on MiniMax/xAI sessions looks like a bug. It's actually the cross-provider guard returning \`null\` (no worker model for unknown provider), which \`expandQuery\` logs as 'timed out or failed'. Fix (PR #622): \`getWorkerModel()\` now echoes the session model for unknown providers instead of returning \`undefined\`, so query expansion works on all providers. The 9-second gap before the log is MiniMax's response latency before the recall tool fires — not a real timeout. Confirmed in production logs (Jun 8 2026): session=0cLYYclt, model=MiniMax-M3, provider=minimax-coding-plan, upstream=https://api.minimax.io/anthropic — turn started 23:22:41, timeout logged 23:22:50 (9s gap), recall follow-up executed 23:23:05. New PID post-merge shows no cross-provider guard events — fix is working.

<!-- lore:019e6950-8200-7473-87a5-45a861bb84af -->
* **recall.ts: unescaped quotes/ellipsis in marker strings cause store miss and raw marker leak**: Trap: \`buildRecallMarker()\` embeds raw \`query\` between double-quotes and raw \`id\` before \`…\` — looks safe because queries are usually plain text. But if \`query\` contains \`"\`, \`MARKER\_REGEX\` (\`/📚 Searching (.+?) for "(.+?)"…/\`) truncates the captured group at the first inner quote; \`recallStoreKey()\` produces a mismatched key; \`store.get(key)\` returns undefined; the marker is left as raw text in the conversation visible to the upstream LLM. Same issue for \`id\` containing \`…\`. Fix: escape \`"\` → \`\\"\` in \`buildRecallMarker()\` and unescape in \`parseRecallMarker()\`; for IDs, percent-encode or strip \`…\` before embedding.

<!-- lore:019ea9ba-ea3f-7bf4-beca-b743b8278bc4 -->

Sample error: StatusCode: non 2xx status code (500 GET https://www.thefastcode.com/en-idr/article/how-to-customize-slack-s-appearance-with-themes). Investigate the root cause — this is a recurring obstacle in this project.

<!-- lore:019e2e20-95b3-7a9d-ab38-77d87eafecc4 -->
* **splitSegments() infinite recursion on oversized single messages**: \`splitSegments()\` infinite recursion on oversized single messages in \`packages/core/src/distillation.ts\`: recurses infinitely when a single message exceeds \`maxSegmentTokens\` (16384). \`findSplitIndex()\` returns \`messages.length\` (=1), so \`left = messages.slice(0, 1)\` produces an identical recursive call. Triggered on large tool outputs (~49KB+). Fix: add base case after the \`totalTokens <= maxTokens\` guard — \`if (messages.length <= 1) return \[messages]\`. The oversized message becomes an indivisible segment.

<!-- lore:019e49d5-15c4-78d1-8bbc-f43fde34d9f1 -->
* **startServer() returns plain object, not Promise — use startGateway() for programmatic async use**: Gateway startup traps: (1) \`startServer()\` returns \`{ stop, port, hosts }\` synchronously — use \`startGateway()\` from \`cli/start.ts\` for \`Promise\<GatewayHandle>\`. (2) \`loadConfig()\` in \`config.ts\` is SYNC — calling \`.then()\` throws TypeError. (3) EADDRINUSE fires as async \`'error'\` event — wrap \`server.listen()\` in a Promise. (4) Use port \`0\` (ephemeral) in tests. (5) \`@loreai/core\` exports async \`load(directory)\` — distinct from gateway's sync \`loadConfig()\`. (6) In-process callers MUST pass \`local:true\` — hosted mode disables FS ops in \`@loreai/core\` (breaks \`getGitRemote()\`, \`.lore.md\` import, config loading). (7) \`lore run\` and \`lore import\` always run locally — both set \`opts.local=true\`.

<!-- lore:019ea9c2-243b-7a62-8c5e-c825bd12534f -->
* **vitest from subdir fails: dist missing for aliased @loreai/core**: Trap: running \`vitest\` from a package subdir fails with "Failed to resolve entry for package @loreai/core" because \`packages/core/dist\` is missing. The repo-root vitest config aliases \`@loreai/core\` → \`packages/core/src\` and \`@loreai/gateway\` → \`packages/gateway/src\` via \`path.resolve(\_\_dirname, ...)\` — alias only works when running vitest from repo root with this config. Pretest hook (\`pnpm --filter @loreai/gateway run bundle\`) only bundles gateway, not core. Fix: build \`packages/core/dist/{node,bun}/index.js\` + \`embedding-worker.js\` before running vitest from root. Looks harmless (alias is "just a path") but is a real pre-existing infrastructure requirement.

<!-- lore:019ea9c2-c4aa-78dd-932b-344907791802 -->
* **vitest test cache isolation: reset before fetchModelData() in each test body**: Trap: \`resetWorkerModelState()\` in \`beforeEach\` looks sufficient for cache isolation, but background fire-and-forget fetches from other tests can repopulate the cache between \`beforeEach\` and the test body's \`await fetchModelData()\`. Fix: add a defensive \`resetWorkerModelState()\` (or \`clearModelDataCache()\`) immediately before each \`await fetchModelData()\` call in the test body, not just in \`beforeEach\`. This was fixed in PR #624.

<!-- lore:019ea9c2-23bb-738c-95ac-737887371a9d -->
* **Zod 4 internals: description on schema not \_def; defaultValue is value not fn**: Zod 4 schema description lives at \`s.description\` (top-level property), NOT \`s.\_def.description\` — \`\_def.description\` is undefined. Default wrapper shape: \`\_def.type === "default"\`, \`\_def.innerType\` (not \`\_def.schema\`), \`\_def.defaultValue\` is the \*\*value itself\*\* (e.g. \`0.25\`), NOT a function — calling \`def.defaultValue()\` throws \`TypeError: def.defaultValue is not a function\`. Numeric checks live on inner type (\`unwrap()\` first), each check is a \`{}\` envelope: \`check.\_zod.def.check\` (string like \`"greater\_than"\`), \`check.\_zod.def.value\`, \`check.\_zod.def.inclusive\`. Checks-array schema's own \`\_def.checks\` is empty for default-wrapped numbers. Object shape: \`\_def.type === "object"\`, \`\_def.shape\` is a direct object (not a function). Array: \`{ type: 'array', element }\`. Record: \`{ type: 'record', keyType, valueType }\`.

<!-- lore:019ea9c2-23c0-740f-b290-5016f2fc4ac5 -->
* **zod-to-json-schema fails on Zod 4 wrapped effects — walk Zod directly**: \`zod-to-json-schema\` 3.25.2 (peer \`^4\`) returns empty \`definitions\` when input is a ZodEffects-wrapped object (LoreConfig). \`$refStrategy: "none"\` flag has no effect, \`name\` arg doesn't help. Decision: abandoned JSON Schema route, walked Zod directly via \`.shape\` + \`.description\` + \`unwrap()\`. Saves 3-4 hours of dead-end debugging. For any future doc-gen work in this repo, walk Zod directly — don't reintroduce zod-to-json-schema. See \[\[generate-config-docs]] pattern in \`scripts/generate-config-docs.ts\`.

### Pattern

<!-- lore:019e56d6-9cca-7a77-aa1a-a5850daef395 -->
* **Gateway test patterns: unit vs integration vs subprocess isolation**: Gateway/OpenCode test patterns — three isolation levels: (1) Unit: import functions directly, build fixtures via \`makeRequest()\`/\`makeUserMsg()\` factories. (2) Integration: \`createHarness()\` starts real server on random port with replay interceptor, provides \`chat()\` + \`queryDB()\`. (3) Subprocess isolation: \`mock.module()\` calls isolated in subprocess files to avoid global cache pollution. OpenCode plugin tests: \`LorePlugin\` + \`createMockClient()\` stubbing \`client.tui.showToast\` and \`client.session.\*\`. \`initPlugin()\` returns \`{hooks, tmpDir, cleanup}\`. DB isolation via root \`bunfig.toml\` preloading \`packages/core/test/setup.ts\`. \`GatewayRequest\` minimal required fields: \`protocol, model, system, messages, tools, stream\`. \`PluginInput\` type does NOT include \`chat\` — access via \`client.app.experimental.chat\`. All packages must be devDependencies — CI enforces with \`pnpm run check:deps\`.

### Preference

<!-- lore:019ea9c1-46aa-7a7a-b693-4cd400a6ed0b -->
* **Always add a --check mode to generators and wire them into CI**: When building code/doc generators, the user wants (1) a dedicated \`--check\` flag that exits non-zero on drift instead of writing, and (2) a corresponding \`check:\*\` script in root \`package.json\` and a CI job that runs it. This pattern ensures generated artifacts stay in sync with their source. Apply whenever creating a generator script (docs, schemas, configs, types, etc.) — add the \`--check\` mode from the start, expose it via \`package.json\`, and add a CI job in \`.github/workflows/ci.yml\` that gates on it.

<!-- lore:019e920f-0876-7aad-a306-8129434a3d6b -->
* **Always embed behavioral directives as code comments to assert invariants**: Behavioral directives: (1) Write invariant assertions as imperative code comments at enforcement points. (2) 🔴 = durable/identity-level facts; 🟡 = session-scoped — never promote 🟡 to 🔴 without explicit confirmation. (3) After bulk type migrations, run typecheck and update ALL affected test files. (4) Review plan before execution — survey tsconfig, package.json, migration status. Enumerate all consumers of shared state before modifying. Prefer surgical minimal-churn. (5) Bug investigation: present numbered hypotheses, cite exact line numbers, quote file comments verbatim. (6) Always update .lore.md alongside every PR. (7) Prefer CLI over raw API. (8) Always address all code review comments (Copilot or human) completely — fix root cause, add missing tests, apply consistent fixes across all files. Fix biome lint/format errors before pushing. (9) Before merging any PR: run critical self-review checking logic flaws, incomplete allowlists, fragile logic, and CI status.

<!-- lore:019ea9c1-83f4-77dd-bebd-1f5c887e9096 -->
* **Always enforce explicit invariants with NEVER/ALWAYS directives**: User consistently states and reinforces system invariants using emphatic 'ALWAYS' and 'NEVER' directives. Examples: 'ALWAYS included even with zero relevance score', 'ALWAYS binds & clears provisional binding', 'always re-emits system as role:system', 'always run locally', 'Never build logic that assumes raw OpenAI format passes through the core pipeline'. When stating these, user marks them HIGH-PRIORITY (🔴) and expects them to be encoded into .lore.md entries so the assistant never violates them across sessions. Each invariant typically names a specific code location, the behavior, and what it overrides. When implementing or modifying affected code, surface and honor these directives proactively rather than waiting to be told.

<!-- lore:019ea9c7-76ca-7211-9c44-b3eb5a16701f -->
* **Always investigate root causes with precise log evidence before accepting conclusions**: When debugging issues, the user systematically reconstructs timelines from log data, identifies discrepancies between expected and actual behavior (e.g., 'WARN line SHOULD fire but doesn't appear'), and refuses to accept surface-level explanations. They cross-reference multiple data points (PIDs, timestamps, code paths, log line counts) to pinpoint exact failure modes. When a finding contradicts the expected code path, they treat it as a 'critical discrepancy' requiring further investigation rather than moving on. Always provide precise evidence (line numbers, timestamps, log excerpts, variable values) and flag when observed behavior contradicts what the code should theoretically do.

<!-- lore:019e9f06-597e-75c0-8f6a-2d2b4c144bc8 -->
* **Always remove all Bun-specific code and build targets**: Always remove all Bun-specific code: delete dist/bun directories, replace Bun APIs (Bun.mmap, Bun.file, Bun.zstdDecompressSync) with Node.js equivalents, remove Bun-specific mocks/test assertions/build targets. Migrate projects from Bun to Node.js and pnpm. Separate migration steps into distinct PRs — each CI-verified. Never add new Bun-specific code. Bun bugs (#18145, #25677, #31158) cause model-init OOM in WASM paths — numThreads=1 avoids pthread paths. \`node:worker\_threads\` works under both Bun and Node; load worker via \`new URL('./worker.ts', import.meta.url)\`; use \`Float32Array\` structured clone; \`worker.unref()\` for clean exit.

<!-- lore:019e9f41-df33-7e3c-a1a5-843a62fcbd64 -->
* **Always use the same provider and never cross-provider**: Same-provider invariant: worker/warmup model ALWAYS uses same provider as session. \`getWorkerModel()\` (worker-model.ts): effectiveProvider = cfg.model?.providerID ?? sessionProviderID ?? 'anthropic'; fallback chain: (1) cfg.model, (2) sessionModelID (any provider — same provider is always safe), (3) WORKER\_DEFAULTS\[effectiveProvider], (4) undefined. For known providers (anthropic, openai), cost-aware defaults downgrade to cheaper models. For unknown providers with expensive models (inputCost >= EXPENSIVE\_MODEL\_THRESHOLD of $1.50/M), \`findCheaperSameProviderModel()\` dynamically searches models.dev cache for a cheaper same-provider alternative; if no cheaper model found or model is already cheap, echoes the session model. Cross-provider guard in pipeline.ts: detects model/upstream provider mismatch at prompt time (including defaultModel vs upstream), calls \`recordWorkerFailure('cross-provider')\` + returns null. Wire protocol resolved from \`resolveProviderRoute(providerID)?.protocol\`, NOT hardcoded. Workers must NEVER fall back to \`config().model\`/\`cfg.model\` — \`const model = input.model\` with NO fallback is correct in curator.ts, distillation.ts, pattern-echo.ts. Any \`?? config().model\` in worker code is a critical bug.

<!-- lore:019ea9c1-6e71-70e6-9ab5-b859df54ff86 -->
* **Execute multi-phase plans sequentially with explicit verification gates between phases**: The user consistently breaks work into numbered phases (Phase 1, 2, 3, 4) with a defined tracker (e.g., quality/PROGRESS.md, todo list) and works through them in order, marking each complete before moving on. Between phases, the user pauses for verification: build checks, typecheck, test runs, grep audits, or manual review of artifacts. When a tool fails (e.g., edit could-not-find-oldstring 3x), the user expects the assistant to debug root causes systematically (whitespace, unicode bytes, line boundaries) and re-verify after fixing rather than skipping ahead. The user also wants scope explicitly narrowed per phase (e.g., marketing scope = 5 edits, leaving quality/\*.md intact as known limitations) rather than sweeping changes.

<!-- lore:019ea9c1-983a-7534-a481-046614bb204b -->
* **Let distil mechanism handle .lore.md instead of hand-editing**: The user consistently treats .lore.md as a curator-managed artifact. After observing that manual appends trigger a reformatting cascade (181→83 lines for ~24 insertions), the user decided to revert manual edits and rely on the conversation-distil mechanism on the next session to capture decisions. When working in sessions that produce architectural/policy decisions, the user expects entries to flow through distil rather than direct file edits. AI assistants should never manually append to .lore.md during a session — instead, surface new decisions verbally and let the curator regenerate the file on next session start. This avoids the 'disappearing entries' trap where existing entries get reformatted on save, making diffs appear to show content loss.

<!-- lore:019e9d98-e22f-7f0d-87d3-91c4f8b9a5e3 -->
* **OpenCode plugin: per-project state map for project path header injection**: OpenCode plugin per-project state: \`projectState\` Map keyed by \`ctx.project.id\` → \`{ projectPath, gitRemote, lastSeenAt }\`; TTL \`SESSION\_STATE\_TTL\_MS = 24h\`. \`reapStaleProjectState()\` called on every new entry. \`chat.headers\` hook uses per-project Map entry to avoid cross-project clobbering. Module-level \`currentProjectPath\`/\`currentGitRemote\` updated on every call — fallback only when hook bypassed. \`loreInitPromise\` memoization prevents concurrent plugin calls racing on probe→spawn. Gateway discovery order: (0) \`LORE\_REMOTE\_URL\`; (1) \`LORE\_GATEWAY\_URL\`; (2) port file (ports 3207, 5673); (3) in-process \`startGateway({ quiet:true, local:true })\`. \`remoteGateway\` auto-detection 4-layer precedence in \`start.ts\`: (1) \`LORE\_REMOTE\_GATEWAY\` env; (2) \`LORE\_HOSTED\_MODE\`; (3) bind address (\`0.0.0.0\`/\`::\` = non-loopback); (4) default=true. \`--local\` CLI flag ALWAYS wins. In-process callers MUST pass \`local:true\`.

<!-- lore:019ea9c2-23d8-7781-af7d-7b8e4fed685c -->
* **Prefer distil-capture over manual .lore.md edits**: \`.lore.md\` is lore-managed — manual edits trigger a reformatting cascade on save (181→83 lines for ~24 insertions observed). The linter re-renders existing entries, making diffs look like content loss when it's just formatting. Going forward: let new decisions get captured via the normal conversation-distil mechanism on the next session, not by hand-editing \`.lore.md\`. The \`.lore.md\` header comment says "manual edits are imported on next session" but the import also re-renders, so manual edits are fragile. See existing entries: \[\[019e2126-a3ff-75f3-8680-5cca2979bfa1]] (capture findings in .lore.md) and \[\[019e25ee-17ac-71c3-9020-30e342b5636e]] (periodic/dirty-flag persistence).

<!-- lore:019ea9bb-d438-73e8-97d7-eabe87531d39 -->
* **Tool Failure**: Recurring tool failures in this project: (1) \`edit\` "other:could-not-find-oldstring" — check whitespace/unicode/line endings exactly; user expects systematic root-cause debugging not skip-ahead. (2) \`plan\_exit\` "the-user-dismissed-this" — user dismisses plan prompts; prefer calling plan\_exit without re-asking. (3) \`webfetch\` non-2xx — frequently blocked on third-party sites. (4) \`read\` not\_found — verify path before retry. (5) \`edit\` aborted — typically transient, retry. The user has explicitly stated: when edit fails 3x, debug root causes (whitespace, unicode bytes, line boundaries) and re-verify after fixing, never skip ahead.

<!-- lore:019ea9ce-2461-77a0-8789-16d164374fa7 -->
* **Verify full CI status before merging, distinguishing required jobs from skipped nightly/release jobs**: When a PR is ready to merge, the user expects the assistant to explicitly enumerate which CI jobs passed, which failed, and which were skipped (nightly/release jobs like Build Nightly Binaries, Generate Release Patches, Publish Nightly to GHCR are expected to skip on PRs). Merge should only be enabled after ALL required jobs (changes, preview, test, binary smoke for darwin-arm64 and windows-x64, CI Status) flip to green. The user also expects local typecheck and lint to be run pre-push, not relied on CI alone. When CI results are shared, acknowledge which jobs are in-progress vs completed before drawing conclusions.
